probes.question: What is the right order of the instruction cycle?
True or false: the CPU follows the fetch-decode-execute cycle from boot-up until the computer shuts down.

image.alt: A microscope photo of an opened CPU showing the silicon die with its many rectangular blocks, gold bond wires and package pins.
image.credit: Thomy pc at German Wikipedia / Wikimedia Commons

panels.text: Under all the apps, a CPU does one thing over and over: the instruction cycle. It runs from boot-up until the computer shuts down.
Fetch. A register called the program counter holds the address of the next instruction. The CPU reads that instruction from memory, and the counter moves on to the one after.
Decode. The control unit works out what the instruction means: which operations and operands are needed, and it signals the parts of the CPU that will do the work.
Execute. The CPU carries it out. Then the cycle starts again with the next instruction.
